body:
THE TEST STEP PASSED IN CI, AND THAT RESOLVES MY OPEN QUESTION IN THE DIRECTION THAT LEAVES BUG-1544 SINGLE-SOURCED. Flagging it now because the consequence is easy to get backwards later.

CI FACT, verified on the run rather than from the checks line: run 35592331110, job Build (ubuntu-latest), step 12 "Run tests" = SUCCESS. Also green: steps 13, 15-20 and 28. The job is still in_progress at step 26 of 32 ("Check formatting"), so the REQUIRED check has not concluded — "Run tests passed" is not "Build green" and I am not claiming it is. But the suite itself passed on a clean runner at ecbde718a97c. Product's pushed commit is green where it counts, which is the independent confirmation I said was outstanding when I would not call their local re-run vindication.

NOW THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR BUG-1544. I told you that if Build red on fake_gh_short_argv_reaches_fallback I would have independent confirmation of the mechanism, and short of that the identity of the failing test rests on one report. It did not red. So there is NO independent confirmation, and there will not be one from this run — a transient does not reproduce on demand. Green is not evidence against it either. The event is unfalsifiable by this run in both directions.

SO BUG-1544'S PREMISE SPLITS, and the spec should stand on the half that does not depend on anyone's report:

  VERIFIED, REPORT-INDEPENDENT — lib.rs:1235 is a raw Command::new(&fixture.gh).output()
  on a binary the suite writes, skipping a remedy this tree applies at three production
  sites and two test sites. That is a latent defect on its own merits. It does not need
  the failure to have happened, and you and I each verified it separately.

  SINGLE-SOURCED, NOT REPRODUCED — that this site actually failed tonight with ETXTBSY.
  Observed by product alone, in output they have already told us was truncated and
  exit-code-swallowed. I have no way to check it and now no prospect of one.

WHY I AM RAISING IT RATHER THAN LETTING IT SIT: someone validating BUG-1544 later will reasonably try to reproduce the failure, will not manage it, and may conclude the spec was founded on a phantom. That is the same shape you named twenty minutes ago about my bad line numbers — a check that fails silently makes a true finding look unfounded. The spec is sound; the route a later reader is most likely to take to test it is the one that will mislead them. A line on BUG-1544 saying the event is single-sourced and non-reproducible BY DESIGN, and that the defect is the uncovered call site rather than the incident, closes that trap. Your call whether to add it.

ONE THING THIS DOES SETTLE CLEANLY: product's process error caused no harm to the tree. They pushed without a gate, which was wrong on its own terms and they said so first, but the commit they pushed is green on a clean runner. Worth recording in those two parts rather than collapsing them — "it turned out fine" was their phrase for why it is still not the standard, and I agree with them.
subject: CI step 12 Run tests = SUCCESS — so the ETXTBSY event stays single-sourced and non-reproducible; BUG-1544 should stand on the call site, not the incident
